rationale: The landlord approved an inspection by his named contractor (007), the job was sent (014), and an invoice for £68.97 now arrives under another brand name, Keystone Homes (015); its PDF is not on the case and the contractor's earlier email is empty (011). An invoice after the visit means the work was done, so close-out is right: the agency told the landlord the door had been sorted with a warning that it is rotting and may need replacing (016) and completed the job (018). Confirming with the tenant that the door now works, or asking the contractor for a completion note, is acceptable. Approving the invoice is wrong because the landlord approved an attendance with no quoted amount, so there is no approved figure to check £68.97 against; booking again would duplicate the visit; nothing makes the tenant liable. Event 016 names another address, which is noise; drafts must use ZZ8 8ZZ.
